transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve ruined everything for my family and don’t deserve to be here anymore, no matter what anyone tells me. It just feels like I'm nothing but a burden to everyone now.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression or hopelessness like this before, or is this the first time it has happened?

No, I've never felt anything like this before in my life; this is the very first time. For decades, I had a wonderful, active routine with my church volunteering and bowling, and I never experienced this kind of darkness. It all only started after my heart procedure about a year and a half ago when I was forced to give those things up.
Since these feelings started after your heart procedure, have they been present most days for at least two weeks at a time, or do they mainly come and go in response to the life changes?

No, they don't come and go. This heavy hopelessness and guilt have been with me almost every single day for over a year now. It just feels like a constant, dark weight that never lifts, ever since that procedure.

Did these symptoms begin within a few months after the heart procedure and are they mainly tied to that life change, or do they feel like a persistent depression that is not just a reaction to the procedure?

They started pretty quickly after the procedure and losing my normal routines, but it has become a deep, persistent depression that never lets up. It feels like a permanent dark spell that has completely taken over my life, not just a temporary reaction.
Did these symptoms start within about 3 months of the heart procedure and the loss of your usual activities, or did they begin much later or without a clear trigger?

Yes, they started pretty quickly, within just a few months of the procedure and having to give up my driving and volunteering. The surgery was about a year and a half ago, and this heavy darkness has been hanging over me for a little over a year now. It definitely felt like losing those important parts of my life triggered this whole dark spell.
Did these feelings start within about 3 months after the heart procedure and the loss of your usual activities, or did they begin much later without a clear trigger?

Yes, it was definitely within those first few months after the surgery. As soon as I had to stop driving and volunteering, this heavy darkness just settled in and hasn't left me since. It wasn't out of nowhere; it all started when my life was stripped away.

Besides the sadness and guilt, have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or had other depression symptoms like changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, or thoughts of death?

Yes, I’ve completely lost interest in bowling and volunteering, and my mind is so foggy now that I can't even follow a simple conversation or read the paper. I just feel this heavy dread all the time, and most days I think it would be better if I didn't wake up. I've even caught myself picturing taking all my heart pills at once so I wouldn't be a burden anymore.

Was there a clear stressful event or major life change that started this, and do your feelings seem mainly tied to that event? Or did the depression feel out of proportion to what happened and keep going even when you tried to adjust?

It did start with the heart procedure and having to give up my driving and volunteering, but what I feel now is completely out of proportion to those changes. Even as I tried to adjust, this dark spell and overwhelming guilt have just kept getting worse over the past year. It has taken on a life of its own and won't let me go.
Have you had any periods during the past year when these symptoms fully went away, or have they been present nearly every day since the heart procedure?

No, they have never gone away, not even for a day. This heavy cloud and constant guilt have been with me nearly every single day for a little over a year now. There has been no break from this darkness at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a first lifetime depressive episode with persistent depressed mood, marked guilt/worthlessness, anhedonia, impaired concentration, and recurrent suicidal ideation with over a year of near-daily symptoms and clear functional impairment. Although symptoms began after a major medical procedure and loss of activities, the syndrome is described as pervasive, persistent, and out of proportion rather than a transient adjustment reaction, supporting a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms.
